title: Teaching to your ‘learning style’ doesn’t seem to help you learn
body: Many people believe they are visual, auditory or kinaesthetic learners who learn best when taught that way. People certainly have preferences, but when researchers test the key claim, that matching teaching to a person’s style improves results, well-designed studies have largely failed to find a benefit. What seems to matter more is matching the method to the material, such as using diagrams for anatomy or audio for pronunciation.

slides.heading: Share of UK academics who said this about learning styles, 2017

items.label: Used it in the past year

slides.note: A 2017 survey of academics in the UK. ‘Matching’: teaching students in their preferred style.
slides.explanation: Nine in ten agreed the theory is flawed, yet 58% still believed matching helps, and a third had used it that year.

slides.question: What seems to matter more than matching teaching to a learner’s style?
options: Matching the method to the material
slides.explanation: Well-designed studies have largely failed to find a benefit from matching styles. Fitting the method to the material, like diagrams for anatomy, seems to matter more.
